newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks lose 1.78 pct on economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks lose 1.78 pct on economic data.

text.p: Thai stocks retreated 1.78 percent on Thursday in response to seasonal tight liquidity and disappointed economic indicators released by the central bank, brokers said.
The SET index, breaking a three-day rallying streak, closed 14.94 points lower at 826.48 on holiday-thinned 2.8 billion baht turnover.
"Investors were disappointed by the widened October trade deficit figure released by the central bank today," said Sanpong Limthamrongkul of Jardine Fleming.
Brokers said investors were also induced to sell by a relatively high October current account deficit which was a touch lower than the September figure.
The central bank said the October deficit narrowed to 30.2 billion baht from 30.5 billion in September, while trade deficit widened sharply to 36.2 billion baht from 25.0 billion.
"Local investors sold ahead of the return of foreigners from their holidays. They pre-empted foreign selling expected early next month because of the disappointing economic data," said Sanpong.
"Tight liquidity in the money market, which caused the overnight interbank rate to surge, was another factor for the selling," Sanpong said.
The overnight interbank rate rose to 14.50 percent late on Thursday from 13.75-14.00 in the morning.
All major sectors declined with the finance sector leading the retreat, falling 4.92 percent.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 3.50 baht to 50, Shinawatra Computer shed 14 to 302.
